name: CRGO Electrical Steel & Transformer Core Localisation
scope: India meets ~90% of its 400-450 kt/yr grain-oriented (CRGO) transformer steel demand from imports (China, Japan, Korea, Russia) while grid capex drives transformer demand; DGTR opened an anti-dumping probe on CRGO and amorphous metal on ~22-24 Jun 2026 on a JSW JFE Electrical Steel petition, and the JSW Steel-JFE JV is expanding Nashik (50 to 250 ktpa, 2028-30) and Vijayanagar (to 100 ktpa, ~2027). Listed exposure is narrow (JSW Steel via an unlisted 50:50 JV; small-cap CRGO core/lamination processors Vilas Transcore and Jay Bee Laminations) and the small caps have de-rated rather than re-rated (Vilas ~+16% in 6 months but ~-20% YoY; Jay Bee ~-61% YoY), so it is early and undiscovered in thematic media, but it overlaps the broader Power & Transmission backlog theme and a duty could squeeze processor margins as well as help domestic steel.
questions: What is CRGO (grain-oriented electrical steel) and amorphous metal, why are they critical to transformers, and how large is India's demand versus domestic supply (demand ~400-450 kt, domestic ~40-50 kt)?

What is the status of the DGTR anti-dumping investigation on CRGO and amorphous metal (initiated Jun 2026, JSW JFE Electrical Steel Nashik as petitioner): scope, timeline, likely duty, Finance Ministry decision, and the GTRI counter-arguments on transformer costs?

What are JSW JFE Electrical Steel's capacity plans (Nashik 50 to 250 ktpa, Vijayanagar to 100 ktpa, investment, commissioning dates) and what share of JSW Steel's value and earnings can this realistically become?

Do any other Indian listed companies produce or plan to produce CRGO or amorphous electrical steel (e.g. other steel majors, thyssenkrupp India, Proterial/Metglas-Shirdi Sai JV) and what is their listed status and confirmed evidence?

What are Vilas Transcore and Jay Bee Laminations doing (CRGO processing capacity of 36,000 and 23,340 MTPA, utilisation, customers, exports, margins, working capital) and how does an import duty or domestic supply shift affect their raw-material cost and margins?

How does BIS licensing of imported CRGO and import uncertainty affect availability and pricing, and who gains or loses from domestic supply versus a duty (steel makers, core processors, transformer makers such as Indo Tech, Voltamp)?
How big is the grid and transformer demand pull (Rs 9 lakh crore grid plan to 2032, renewable integration, data centres) and the timeline over which domestic CRGO capacity can meet it?

Has the market already priced this in: 6-month and 1-year stock performance of JSW Steel, Vilas Transcore and Jay Bee, plus the extent of broker, mainstream media and retail finance coverage naming these stocks as a CRGO theme?

What are the key risks: duty rejected or diluted, long commissioning delays to 2028-30, raw-material price volatility squeezing processors, tiny market caps and liquidity, and JSW Steel's CRGO exposure being immaterial to its consolidated earnings?

What near-term catalysts exist: DGTR preliminary findings, Ministry of Finance duty notification, Vijayanagar commissioning in 2027, Nashik furnace delivery, and Q2/Q3 FY27 results for the processors?

electrical_steel_makers: Listed companies making or building CRGO / amorphous electrical steel capacity, directly or through a JV
core_processors: Listed companies slitting, cutting and assembling CRGO into transformer laminations and cores, expanding capacity
